es.summary: Trastorno genético de hipermetabolismo muscular desencadenado por anestésicos volátiles o succinilcolina, que produce aumento rápido de la temperatura corporal y crisis sistémica.
key_points: Es una emergencia intraoperatoria que requiere diagnóstico y tratamiento en minutos.
El dantroleno es el fármaco de elección para revertir la crisis.
Se asocia a hiperpotasemia, acidosis metabólica y rabdomiólisis.
Control estricto de la temperatura, ventilación y volumen intravascular es esencial.
Los pacientes deben ser identificados preoperatoriamente y se debe disponer de dantroleno en el quirófano.

pathophysiology: Mutación en el receptor de rianodina (RYR1) o CACNA1S produce liberación descontrolada de Ca2+ del retículo sarcoplásmico.
El exceso de Ca2+ genera hipercontracción muscular y aumento del consumo de O2.
Se produce generación de calor, acidosis láctica y liberación de potasio y CK al torrente sanguíneo.
risk_factors: Historia familiar de HM o prueba de contractura muscular.
Uso de anestésicos volátiles (sevoflurano, desflurano) o succinilcolina.
Edad pediátrica o juvenil, mayor susceptibilidad muscular.
signs_symptoms: Aumento rápido de la temperatura corporal > 38 °C, a menudo > 41 °C.
Rigidez muscular, especialmente de la mandíbula (trismo).
Hipercapnia, aumento de la presión end‑tidal de CO2.
diagnostics: Monitorización continua de temperatura, EtCO2 y gases arteriales.
treatment: Administrar dantroleno IV 2.5 mg/kg, repetir cada 5‑10 min hasta control.
Ventilación mecánica con 100 % O2 para corregir hipoxia e hipercapnia.
Enfriamiento activo: bolsas de hielo, mantas refrigerantes, lavado con agua fría.
Reemplazo de líquidos con solución cristaloide fría; monitorizar diuresis.
Tratar hiperpotasemia con gluconato de calcio, insulina‑glucosa y diuréticos.
complications: Coagulopatía por consumo de factores y DIC.
Muerte si no se trata rápidamente.
nursing_care: Evaluar temperatura cada minuto y registrar cambios.
Monitorear EtCO2, presión arterial, frecuencia cardíaca y saturación de O2.
Mantener vía aérea segura; aspirar secreciones y observar rigidez facial.
Registrar diuresis y balance hídrico; administrar líquidos fríos según orden.
Preparar y administrar dantroleno según protocolo; observar respuesta clínica.
patient_teaching: Informar al paciente y familia sobre la predisposición genética y la necesidad de informar a futuros anestesiólogos.
Explicar la importancia de llevar una tarjeta de alerta de HM.
Enseñar signos de rigidez muscular y fiebre postoperatoria que requieren atención inmediata.
Reforzar la necesidad de evitar anestésicos desencadenantes en procedimientos futuros.

outcomes: CK sérica < 200 U/L dentro de 24 h

interventions.action: Monitorear electrolitos séricos cada 30 min durante la crisis y cada 4 h después.
interventions.rationale: Detectar y corregir rápidamente hiperpotasemia y otras alteraciones.

interventions.action: Administrar dantroleno según protocolo y registrar tiempo de respuesta.
interventions.rationale: Detener la liberación de Ca2+ y reducir el metabolismo muscular.

interventions.action: Aplicar enfriamiento activo y registrar temperatura corporal cada minuto.
interventions.rationale: Disminuir la producción de calor y prevenir daño tisular.

interventions.action: Iniciar hidratación con solución cristaloide fría y monitorizar diuresis cada hora.
interventions.rationale: Mantener perfusión renal y favorecer la eliminación de CK y potasio.

interventions.action: Administrar gluconato de calcio IV si K+ > 5.5 mEq/L o arritmia presente.
interventions.rationale: Estabilizar la membrana cardíaca y prevenir arritmias.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de perfusión tisular cerebral ineficaz

interventions.action: Controlar presión arterial invasiva cada 5 min y ajustar fluidos o vasopresores según necesidad.
interventions.rationale: Garantizar perfusión cerebral adecuada.

interventions.action: Mantener ventilación con FiO2 100 % y ajustar Vt para mantener PaCO2 35‑45 mmHg.
interventions.rationale: Prevenir hipoxia e hipercapnia que comprometen la perfusión cerebral.

interventions.action: Aplicar enfriamiento activo rápido y registrar temperatura rectal cada minuto.
interventions.rationale: Reducir la demanda metabólica cerebral.

interventions.action: Evaluar nivel de conciencia cada 5 min usando la escala de Glasgow.
interventions.rationale: Detectar deterioro neurológico precoz.

interventions.action: Administrar analgésicos y sedantes leves según orden para evitar agitación que eleve la presión intracraneal.
interventions.rationale: Minimizar aumento de consumo de O2 cerebral.

en.summary: A genetic disorder of muscle hypermetabolism triggered by volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine, causing rapid rise in body temperature and systemic crisis.
key_points: It is an intraoperative emergency requiring diagnosis and treatment within minutes.
Dantrolene is the drug of choice to reverse the crisis.
It is associated with hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, and rhabdomyolysis.
Strict control of temperature, ventilation, and intravascular volume is essential.
Patients should be identified preoperatively and dantrolene must be available in the operating room.

pathophysiology: Mutation in the ryanodine receptor (RYR1) or CACNA1S leads to uncontrolled release of Ca2+ from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
Excess Ca2+ causes muscle hypercontraction and increased O2 consumption.
Heat generation, lactic acidosis, and release of potassium and CK into the bloodstream occur.
risk_factors: Family history of MH or positive contracture test.
Use of volatile anesthetics (sevoflurane, desflurane) or succinylcholine.
Pediatric or young age, higher muscle susceptibility.
signs_symptoms: Rapid rise in body temperature > 38 °C, often > 41 °C.
Muscle rigidity, especially of the jaw (trismus).
diagnostics: Continuous monitoring of temperature, EtCO2, and arterial blood gases.
treatment: Administer dantrolene IV 2.5 mg/kg, repeat every 5‑10 min until controlled.
Mechanical ventilation with 100 % O2 to correct hypoxia and hypercapnia.
Active cooling: ice packs, cooling blankets, cold water lavage.
Replace fluids with cold crystalloid solution; monitor urine output.
Treat hyperkalemia with calcium gluconate, insulin‑glucose, and diuretics.
complications: Coagulopathy from factor consumption and DIC.
nursing_care: Assess temperature every minute and record changes.
Monitor EtCO2, blood pressure, heart rate, and O2 saturation.
Maintain airway security; suction secretions and observe facial rigidity.
Record urine output and fluid balance; administer cold fluids as ordered.
Prepare and administer dantrolene per protocol; observe clinical response.
patient_teaching: Inform patient and family about genetic predisposition and the need to inform future anesthesiologists.
Explain the importance of carrying an MH alert card.
Teach signs of muscle rigidity and postoperative fever that require immediate attention.
Emphasize the need to avoid triggering anesthetics in future procedures.

interventions.action: Monitor serum electrolytes every 30 min during crisis and every 4 h afterward.
interventions.rationale: Detect and correct hyperkalemia and other abnormalities quickly.

interventions.action: Administer dantrolene per protocol and record response time.
interventions.rationale: Stop Ca2+ release and reduce muscle metabolism.

interventions.action: Apply active cooling and record body temperature every minute.
interventions.rationale: Reduce heat production and prevent tissue damage.

interventions.action: Initiate hydration with cold crystalloid solution and monitor urine output hourly.
interventions.rationale: Maintain renal perfusion and facilitate elimination of CK and potassium.

interventions.action: Administer IV calcium gluconate if K+ > 5.5 mEq/L or arrhythmia present.
interventions.rationale: Stabilize cardiac membrane and prevent arrhythmias.

care_plans.diagnosis: Risk for ineffective cerebral tissue perfusion

interventions.action: Control invasive blood pressure every 5 min and adjust fluids or vasopressors as needed.
interventions.rationale: Ensure adequate cerebral perfusion.

interventions.action: Maintain ventilation with FiO2 100 % and adjust tidal volume to keep PaCO2 35‑45 mmHg.
interventions.rationale: Prevent hypoxia and hypercapnia that compromise cerebral perfusion.

interventions.action: Apply rapid active cooling and record rectal temperature every minute.
interventions.rationale: Reduce cerebral metabolic demand.

interventions.action: Assess level of consciousness every 5 min using the Glasgow Coma Scale.
interventions.rationale: Detect early neurological deterioration.

interventions.action: Administer analgesics and light sedatives as ordered to avoid agitation that raises intracranial pressure.
interventions.rationale: Minimize increase in cerebral O2 consumption.

summary.0.quote: Malignant hyperthermia is a rare, potentially life-threatening genetic predisposition to uncontrolled muscle breakdown (hypermetabolism) typically triggered by certain anesthetic medications, most commonly inhalant medications and muscle relaxants.

key_points.1.quote: Meanwhile, other perioperative team members should quickly obtain the MH cart and begin reconstituting dantrolene sodium (e.g., Dantrium, Ryanodex), the specific antidote for MH.

key_points.2.quote: The MH reaction presents with a cascade of symptoms, including masseter muscle rigidity, hyperkalemia, and muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis).

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: During the preoperative assessment, the RN circulator should ask the patient if they or any immediate family member has ever had a problem with anesthesia.

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: Another indication of MH susceptibility is a history of a muscular or neuromuscular disorder (e.g., muscular dystrophy).

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: The MH reaction presents with a cascade of symptoms, including masseter muscle rigidity, hyperkalemia, and muscle breakdown (rhabdomyolysis).

sections.treatment.2.quote: Other team members institute prompt cooling measures: administer cold IV fluids; pack the patient’s neck and head, groin, axilla, and any open cavities with ice; change the forced-air blanket to cool air; and provide supportive care, which is crucial for successful MH management.

sections.complications.4.quote: This results in a hypermetabolic reaction during which body heat can reach beyond life-sustaining temperatures (e.g., 106°F [41.1°C]), which can quickly lead to organ damage and death if not recognized and treated immediately.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: The surgeon and anesthesia provider inform the patient and family members of the event and counsel first-degree family members to undergo genetic testing for MH susceptibility.

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: Recognize cues: Identify the key signs and symptoms of MH (e.g., masseter muscle rigidity, metabolic acidosis, and extremely high temperature [e.g., 106°F {41.1°C}]).
